sections.h2: What makes Fort Lauderdale property different from the rest of Broward?
sections.html:
Water, mostly. The city counts 165 miles of inland waterways, which is how it earned the nickname "Venice of America," and boasts over 3,000 sunny hours yearly. Its Riverwalk anchors an arts and science district with the Broward Center for the Performing Arts, the Museum of Discovery and Science, and the Museum of Art, while Las Olas Boulevard serves as the dining and shopping spine.

Downtown also hosts Broward College, Florida Atlantic University, the Broward County Main Library, and federal, county and school district offices. The city's own profile lists marine trades, manufacturing, finance, insurance, real estate, avionics and aerospace, and film and television among its industries. Houses near water, and the condos along it, are the parcels the appraiser values most closely.

sections.h2: Why is the city called Fort Lauderdale, and how big is it?
sections.html:
From a Second Seminole War stockade built beside the New River in 1838. Major William Lauderdale led Tennessee Volunteers down the east coast that year, and three forts bore his name: one at the fork of the New River, one at Tarpon Bend and the largest on the beach where Bahia Mar sits now. None of them still stands.

The city incorporated on March 27, 1911. It covers roughly 36 square miles and, by the city's own estimate, about 186,220 people, making it the largest of Broward County's 31 municipalities and one of the ten largest in Florida.

sections.h2: What do Census numbers reveal about local housing?
sections.html:
QuickFacts shows 188,677 people as of July 2025, a 3.3 percent gain since 2020, and 80,999 households over 2020 to 2024. Housing details:

  • Owner-occupancy rate: 54.1 percent.
  • Median value of an owned home: $486,700.
  • Monthly owner costs: $2,679 mortgaged, $1,122 unmortgaged.
  • Gross rent, median: $1,854.
  • Population 65 and older: 19.6 percent.

The large senior share makes the low-income senior exemption relevant, and the large renter share means many tax bills go to landlords rather than residents.

sections.h2: Which county desks touch a Fort Lauderdale bill?
sections.html:
City hall does not value or bill property. Valuation and exemption review sit with the appraiser (main line 954-357-6830, exemption help 954-357-5579, office at 1801 NW 49 Street, Suite PA1), while billing sits with the tax collector (954-357-4829).

The appraiser stresses it mails no bills. Filing a deed happens at the county Recording Office, 115 S. Andrews Avenue, Room 114 (954-831-4000).

sections.h2: Which dates run a Fort Lauderdale owner's year?
sections.html:
Statewide timing governs, and Broward layers its own exemption filing periods on top.

Annual property tax rhythm for a Fort Lauderdale parcel
WhenWhat happens
January 1Value and residency are measured
March 1On-time exemption filing ends
AugustTRIM notice mailed
25 days after the noticeValue petition deadline
NovemberBills issued, top discount begins
April 1Delinquency begins

Source: Florida Department of Revenue and Broward County Property Appraiser. The early-pay discount drops one point per month after November.

sections.h2: How long can a Broward owner take to file homestead?
sections.html:
The appraiser's on-time period for 2027 opened March 3, 2026 and closes March 1, 2027, open to people who owned the home and made it their permanent residence after January 1, 2026. A miss is survivable: late filing runs to September 20, 2027, and the appraiser cites section 196.011(8) to explain that nothing, good cause included, extends that date. For 2026, the late period closed September 18, 2026.

Bring Florida identification, either voter registration or a power or water bill in an owner's name, and, for trust ownership, a notarized certificate of trust or the full instrument. Filing online is at bcpa.net/onlinehomestead.asp; paper forms may be emailed, faxed or mailed.

sections.h2: What does the basic exemption actually save in Broward?
sections.html:
For 2026 the appraiser puts the saving at $673 to $1,020 per qualifying home worth $75,000 or more, with the spread coming from different city millage rates. State materials describe the exemption as a $50,000 maximum, where the first $25,000 applies to school taxes and the remainder to other levies.

The cap on homestead assessed value follows the lesser of 3 percent and inflation; the state chart gives 2.7 percent for 2026. Non-homestead parcels have a 10 percent ceiling. Each cap restarts at sale, which is why a buyer's first bill can look nothing like the seller's.

sections.h2: Which other exemptions does Broward list?
sections.html:
Each has its own paperwork, and the appraiser invites calls at 954-357-6830.

  • Low-income seniors: aged 65 on January 1, with homestead and income below the appraiser's printed cap of $38,686, adjusted yearly. Filing runs January 1 to March 1.
  • $5,000 breaks for disability, blindness and widowed owners.
  • A $5,000 veterans' disability break, and a complete exemption for total and permanent disability tied to service.
  • A granny flat exemption for a permitted addition housing a parent or grandparent aged 62 or older, capped at 20 percent of homestead value.
  • Historic property exemptions.

sections.h2: What if I think the Fort Lauderdale value is wrong?
sections.html:
Start with a phone call, because clerical errors often get fixed informally. Failing that, file a petition with the clerk in the 25 days after the August notice. A denied exemption instead goes before the Value Adjustment Board, on a 30 day clock from the denial letter.

Board support staff work from 1801 NW 49th Street (954-357-7205 or 954-357-5444) and handle disagreements over exemptions, classifications and valuations.

sections.h2: What should a seller confirm before putting the house on the market?
sections.html:
• Search the parcel on the property appraiser's website and test each exemption shown against how you really use the house.
  • After storm damage that left the house uninhabitable 30 days or more, the appraiser accepts a catastrophic structural damage report.
  • Decide whether this year's bill gets paid now or from closing proceeds.
  • Report any rental use accurately, since renting can end homestead.
  • Ask the collector how a deferral or installment plan behaves if you sell.

Because under 55 percent of homes are owner-occupied, a fair number of sellers are landlords, and for them rental and business property questions sit alongside the homestead ones.

sections.h2: Is there a way to postpone or split the bill?
sections.html:
Two routes exist. Deferral, through Form DR-570 filed by March 31, postpones the portion exceeding 5 percent of household income, all of it if income is under $10,000, and the threshold is 3 percent for permanent residents 65 or older. Installments require an application to the collector by May 1.

Either way, the August notice shows what is coming.

sections.h2: What stays with me and what goes to the buyer at sale?
sections.html:
The Broward appraiser's home page tells buyers not to assume the seller's tax continues: a change of ownership resets assessed value to full market value. Exemptions stay behind, so the buyer applies anew. What you can carry is accumulated Save Our Homes savings, through portability to a new Florida homestead started inside a three year window; the appraiser offers a portability estimator for that. The exemption itself never moves.

The closing agent prorates the year's tax. Separately, the appraiser runs a free Owner Alert that notifies you if a document changing ownership of your property reaches its office.

faqs.q: When is a Fort Lauderdale tax bill due?
faqs.a: Bills are issued in November, and a balance still open on April 1 turns delinquent. The largest discount rewards November payment and fades by February.

faqs.q: Where does a Fort Lauderdale homeowner apply for homestead?
faqs.a: With the Broward appraiser, online or on paper. The on-time deadline is March 1, and 2027 late filings stop September 20, 2027.

faqs.q: Does the city assess my house?
faqs.a: No. Broward's appraiser values it and Broward's collector bills it; the city is only one of the taxing bodies listed.

faqs.q: Can I contest a Fort Lauderdale assessment?
faqs.a: Yes. Petition the clerk during the 25 days after the August notice, or use the Value Adjustment Board for a denied exemption. A call to the appraiser first often resolves errors.

faqs.q: Can renting out the house cost me the exemption?
faqs.a: It can. The exemption rests on permanent residence, so full-time rental use may end eligibility. Report changes in use to the appraiser.
